Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As we begin our security review for a potential integration, our InfoSec team asked that I follow up with a few targeted HIPAA items so we can complete our DPIA and procurement checklist:

1) BAA scope: can Redwood sign a BAA covering processing of PHI for our production and staging environments? If there are environment exclusions (e.g., analytics sandboxes or public hosted tiers), please list them.

2) PHI types: confirm whether Redwood ever persists PHI in logs, crash reports, or telemetry (PII vs PHI). If so, what redaction/DLP controls are in place?

3) Audit logs: we need a one-week sample export (anonymized) showing authentication events, admin actions, and model access events tied to request IDs. Please indicate retention windows for audit logs and whether exports are possible via API or require support.

4) DPIA inputs: for our privacy team, can you provide a short data flow diagram and whether Redwood’s hosted offering requires SCCs or other transfer mechanisms for EU-origin PHI?

Attached is our standard checklist — we tried to mark the highest-priority items. Can you get back to us by EOD Thursday? If any of this requires legal/security review on your side, happy to give you extra time; please indicate estimated turnaround.

Best,
Oliver Kim

Hi Oliver — thanks for the detailed list and for the checklist. Quick answers inline to get you started; I’m looping in Karthik from Security for the technical artifacts (audit export + data flow diagram) and Legal for the BAA wording.

1) BAA scope: Redwood is able to sign a standard BAA for our Dedicated and Private deployments. Our shared hosted offering (public multi-tenant) is not eligible for BAA coverage by default — exceptions require a Dedicated tenancy or Private deployment. Karthik, please confirm exact env names and any caveats for staging/non-prod.

2) PHI in telemetry/logs: we do not intentionally persist raw PHI in system telemetry. We do collect request metadata (request_id, model_id, timestamps) and may persist a hashed or truncated client-provided identifier for debugging. We have an automated redaction pipeline for user-submitted content in crash reports and telemetry ingestion.

3) Audit logs: we can produce admin/authentication and model-access audit exports. Retention: default hosted retention is 90 days; Dedicated customers can configure longer retention (contract-dependent). Exports are available via the Console export UI and via our admin API for Dedicated/Private customers. I’ll attach a one-week sanitized sample export from a similar Dedicated tenancy.

4) DPIA/data transfers: for EU-origin PHI, Private deployments keep data in-customer VPC so SCCs aren’t required. For Hosted customers, we rely on SCCs and appropriate data processing addenda; our legal team can share the DPA/SCC pack.

We’ll follow up with the data flow diagram and sample logs by EOD Wednesday. If you need the BAA sooner, let us know and we’ll prioritize Legal.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Oliver — Karthik from Redwood Security here. Apologies for the slight delay; we assembled the artifacts requested. Summary below and attached are the sanitized examples: Redwood_HIPAA_BAA_DPIA_ReqChecklist.pdf (our annotated checklist) and audit-log-sample.csv (anonymized entries).

- BAA coverage: Redwood will execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted multi-tenant customers are not eligible by default. Staging environments that are configured within a Dedicated tenancy are covered; separate public staging in the shared hosted tier is excluded. Legal (cc’d) can provide the standard BAA template and an addendum if needed for non-standard retention terms.

- PHI handling: we do not intentionally retain unredacted PHI in telemetry, crash reports, or standard logs. Our ingestion pipeline applies pattern-based redaction for common PHI classes (SSNs, MRNs, DOB formats) and we provide customers with options to disable telemetry capture in Dedicated/Private setups.

- Audit logs: attached is a sanitized 7-day export showing: timestamp, event_type (auth/login, admin:update, model:invoke), actor_id (hashed), resource_id, request_id, and outcome. Note the sample is anonymized and the full export for a specific tenant can include IPs and session IDs depending on customer contract. Retention: 90 days default for hosted; longer retention available under Dedicated contracts (up to 5 years by arrangement). Exports: Console UI export (CSV) and Admin API endpoint (/v1/admin/audit/export) for Dedicated/Private — public hosted requires support ticket.

- DPIA inputs & transfers: For EU data subjects, Private deployments keep data in-customer VPC (no cross-border transfers for processing). For hosted customers with EU-origin data, transfers are covered by our DPA + SCC framework; Legal can provide the SCC annex and help with Supplementary Measures.

Next steps: 
- I attached the data flow diagram (high-level) and an annotated checklist. 
- If HealthNexus needs a tailored BAA for staging/analytics coverage, Legal will review scope and provide redlines.

Oliver — happy to jump on a quick 30-min call if you want us to walk through the export columns or the diagram.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference
